commits.subject: core: rewrite POSIX RunRedirect() from popen() to fork/execve - fix #463
commits.body:
- popen() runs /bin/sh -c and records the shell pid: killing it on
abort leaves the actual worker as an orphan re-parented to PID 1
(as reported for TSynAngelize) - the child now runs in its own
setsid() group, so the whole process group is signaled on abort
- fix EOF busy-spin regression introduced by 7ec04e578 (n<0 vs n<=0):
since 2023/01 any RunRedirect() call with INFINITE waitfordelayms
would never return once the process ended, burning 100% CPU on a
poll(POLLHUP)/read()=0 tight loop - proven by strace
- simple commands are resolved and executed with no shell at all,
with a shell fallback e.g. for built-ins - the executable lookup
uses the PATH= actually supplied to execve() via RunEnvPath(), not
the parent PATH
- new RunFork() shared helper keeps the vfork() behavior with libc
on BSD/SunOS, as RunInternal() and the FPC RTL POpen_internal();
the child side is strictly limited to low-level syscalls, checking
the failures which would break redirection
- env/options parameters are now honored (were silently ignored)
- wrkdir now applies to the child process only - it used to ChDir()
the whole calling process, and never restore it
- exitcode^ is now the actual WaitProcess() result, or -1 if aborted
- the child environment is prepared before fork() for fork-safety,
also fixing RunInternal() E2BIG path which could return in the child
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: core: add TDebugFile.StackTrace() methods - request #401
commits.body:
- return the current thread stack trace as convenient text, with no
exception involved - e.g. for diagnostic endpoints or error reporting
- TSynLog.AddStackTrace now shares the very same implementation on FPC,
with byte-identical log output (verified A/B on aarch64-linux)
- the use: TSynLogStackTraceUse parameter follows the TSynLogFamily
semantics: ignored on FPC, and stOnlyManual is implemented on Delphi
Win32 via the manual ebp-chain walk shared with TSynLog.AddStackManual
- the manual scan never reads its own output frames[] buffer, and sets
tiExceptionIgnore so its speculative reads don't reach the logs
- validated on FPC 3.2.3 (x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, win32, win64)
and Delphi 13 (win32 including stOnlyManual at runtime, win64)
- note: on FPC, frame availability follows the RTL CaptureBacktrace()
constraints - the calling code needs stack frames on x86_64
($STACKFRAMES ON), whereas the aarch64 ABI keeps a frame pointer
commits.author: zen010101
